newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH 1998 BUDGET SUPPORTS FISCAL TARGETS - GOVT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH 1998 BUDGET SUPPORTS FISCAL TARGETS - GOVT.

text.p: The Finnish government said on Friday its 1998 state budget proposal aimed to bring the rise in state indebtedness to a halt and improve employment conditions.

"The government aims at economic stability, at halting the rise in central government indebtedness and at improved conditions to take care of employment," the left-right-green coalition said in a statement.

"The budget proposal supports the government's fiscal objectives -- a sustained reduction of the deficit of the central government finances, and turning the debt ratio (state debt to GDP) into decline," it said.
Fiscal austerity and low inflation were contributing to low interest rates, which in turn supported economic growth and jobs creation, it said.

Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen told a news conference that the government had agreed to target a balanced budget and that "a budget surplus, or at least in balance, is already in sight there around the turn of the millenium".
Asked whether this meant already in 1999, Lipponen said: "I dare not say when at this stage, hopefully before 2000."
Lipponen also said the budget process had further united the government, and all five coalition parties' leading ministers said at the news conference that the budget was at least satisfactory.
"It brought further unity in government," Lipponen said.
